questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Gulliver easily pulled all the warships of the enemy after him

options.text: All the warships of the enemy had been easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
All the warships of the enemy were easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
All the warships of the enemy were being easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
All the warships of Gulliver were easily pulled by the enemy after him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**All the warships of the enemy were easily pulled by Gulliver after him**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'Gulliver' is the subject and ''**all the warships of the enemy**'' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject 'Guliver' of the active voice becomes the object, the object ''all the warships of the enemy'' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "'were + V3 (pulled)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2*.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

questions.question:
**Directions: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

The publics are not satisfied with the new act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The publics are' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the plural noun 'publics' and the **plural verb 'are'** is incorrect.
 
• The noun '**public**' is an **uncountable noun or singular noun**.
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the noun 'public' should be used **in place of** the plural form 'publics'.
 
• Also, we know that a **singular noun or subject always takes a singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the **singular form of the verb 'is'** should be used **in place of** the **plural verb 'are'**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: *The **public is** not satisfied with the new act*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number singular or plural.
 
• If a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural.

• The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
 
 
• The commas, inverted commas are removed, and 'that' is added.

• The simple present tense format 'Subject + V1 (will) + Object' will be changed into the simple past tense format 'Subject + V2 (would) + Object'.

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. The cable was thick as packthread, and the bars were the size of knitting needles.

B. Then I made fifty hooks by twisting three bars together at a time.

C. I ordered a great quantity of strong cable and bars of iron.

D. I twisted the cables together and made fifty strong cords.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CADB'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence 'C' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about "**strong cable and bars of iron**". Hence, 'C' is the first part.
 
• The noun "cable" mentioned in the sentence 'A' refers back to the "strong cable'' mentioned in the sentence 'C'. Hence, 'A' follows 'C'.
 
• The word "twisted" mentioned in the sentence 'D' is linked with the word ''**packthread**'' mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding sentence. Hence, 'B' is the last sentence.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *I ordered a great quantity of strong cable and bars of iron. The cable was thick as pack-thread, and the bars were the size of knitting needles. I twisted the cables together and made fifty strong cords. Then I made fifty hooks by twisting three bars together at a time.*

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

• Example: *Cows and sheep are **herbivores***.
 
 
 
• 'Carnivore' is **an animal that feeds on other animals**.
 
 
• Example: *The Kodiak grizzly bear is the world's largest land **carnivore***.
 
 'Insectivore' is **an animal that feeds on insects, worms, and other invertebrates**.

 
 
• Example: *It is related to the hedgehog, or rather it belongs to the same family of **insectivores***.
 
 
 
• 'Omnivore' is **an animal or person that eats a variety of food of both plant and animal origin**.
 
 
• Example: *Vegetarian and **omnivore** parents had varying influences on dietary intake and biochemical measurements of their children*.

 
 
 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.*

questions.question:
**Directions: **Rearrange the given para jumbled sentences in the correct order.

A. In December 2019, Typhoon Kammuri came to the Philippines.

B. They closed schools and evacuated hundreds of thousands of people from their homes.

C. Officials closed the international airport in the capital city of Manila for 12 hours.

D. It flooded streets and damaged many houses and power lines.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ADCB'.

__
 
• The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about "**Typhoon Kammuri**". Hence, 'A' is the first part.
 
• The pronoun "It" mentioned in the sentence 'D' refers back to the "Typhoon Kammuri'' mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The phrase "**closed the international airport**" mentioned in the sentence 'C' is linked with the word ''**flooded**'' mentioned in the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'C' follows 'D'.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding sentence. Hence, 'B' is the last sentence.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *In December 2019, Typhoon Kammuri came to the Philippines. It flooded streets and damaged many houses and power lines. questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

While my __parents talked__ to the visitor, I made tea in the kitchen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'parents were talking'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the use of the simple past tense 'talked' is incorrect.
 
• The given sentence is in the past continuous tense as it is used to describe something that was happening continuously in the past when another action interrupted it.
 
• The **past continuous tense** is formed by **combining** the past tense of to be (**was/were**) with the **verb’s present participle** (**-ing** word).
 
• Therefore, the past continuous tense ''were talking'' should be used **in place of** the simple past tense 'talked'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: *While my **parents were talking** to the visitor, I made tea in the kitchen*.

• 'Pursued' means **to seek to attain or accomplish a goal over a long period**.
